exposure: Patients who had vaginal delivery vs. cesarean section
Patients admitted for obstetric reasons vs. non-obstetric reasons
cohort: 291 obstetric patients during pregnancy and puerperium from four Finnish university hospitals
finding: While obstetric ICU patients generally have a good probability of recovery and short length of stay, those admitted for non-obstetric reasons and having had a vaginal delivery had higher severity of illness scores, organ failure scores, and levels of intervention.
mod_finding: Patients who had a vaginal delivery had higher severity of illness scores, organ failure scores, and levels of intervention compared to those who delivered by cesarean section.
